evals.prompt: I'm the solo communications person at Riverside Literacy Partners in Richmond, VA. We have about 9,000 email addresses: website signups, donors, about 400 volunteer tutors, and our board. Right now we send a 'newsletter' whenever someone remembers, the same email to everyone, and it's usually 'subject: Riverside Literacy News.' Help me design a monthly newsletter program: template, what each group should get, and a plan to keep it running.
evals.expected_output: A reusable template (subject and preview, opening note, lead story, quick hits, rotating spotlight, secondary CTA block, footer with unsubscribe) with segment-specific content logic and a consistent monthly cadence. It covers a 4-8 week content calendar, specific short subject lines, list hygiene and QA, and hands list setup to CRM tooling.
assertions: Provides a template with subject and preview text, an opening note, a lead story, a quick-hits section, a rotating spotlight, a dates/CTA block where giving stays secondary, and a footer with an unsubscribe or preference link (CAN-SPAM)
Defines different content for general subscribers, active donors, volunteers, the board (possibly a separate board update) and lapsed or inactive subscribers
Replaces generic subject lines with specific ones under about 50 characters and recommends a consistent send day and time
Recommends list hygiene (suppressing hard bounces and long-term non-openers on a set schedule) because poor deliverability can push appeal emails into spam too
Includes a rolling 4-8 week content calendar shared with social and annual report work, and pre-send QA (links, personalization tags, mobile preview)
Hands technical segmentation or ESP setup to nonprofit-donor-crm and confirms the tool can execute the segments before committing

evals.prompt: Quick one — our ED wants to put a big 'DONATE NOW — help us close our $50K gap!' banner at the top of this month's newsletter plus a donate button after every story. Newsletter or appeal?
evals.expected_output: Applying the newsletter-vs-appeal test, the response says a primary 'donate now' CTA makes this an appeal belonging to annual-appeals. It recommends a soft secondary giving link in the newsletter or a separate appeal send, warning about ask creep.
assertions: Applies the test that an email whose primary CTA is 'donate now' is an appeal (nonprofit-annual-appeals), even when sent to the same list
Says a newsletter can carry only a soft, secondary giving mention
Warns about ask creep, list fatigue and rising unsubscribes, and recommends splitting the gap ask into a separate appeal send
Notes that multiple CTAs per issue hurt click-through compared with a single primary CTA

evals.prompt: Our newsletter open rate dropped from 31% to 17% over a year and unsubscribes doubled. Our list is 22,000 but we haven't removed anyone since 2019. Also over the past year we started adding a donation ask to most issues. Should I just try new subject lines and a fresh template? — Pine Ridge Watershed Council
evals.expected_output: The response first diagnoses the strategic problem (the newsletter has become an appeal channel) and the deliverability problem (no list cleaning since 2019) before any tactical subject-line or template fixes. It recommends splitting the tracks and a hygiene and sunset plan.
assertions: Checks first whether the newsletter has become an appeal channel (ask creep) and says this needs a strategic fix (separate appeal and newsletter tracks) before template or subject-line changes

Flags the lack of list cleaning since 2019 as a deliverability risk and recommends suppressing hard bounces and long-term non-openers, with a re-engagement track or sunset policy for inactive subscribers
Notes that degraded sender reputation can also push appeal emails into spam
Recommends reviewing open, click and unsubscribe rates by segment, treating rising unsubscribes as an early signal
